functionRows.title: GOVERN
functionRows.text: The organization’s cybersecurity risk management strategy, expectations, and policy are established, communicated, and monitored

functionRows.title: IDENTIFY
functionRows.text: The organization’s current cybersecurity risks are understood

functionRows.title: PROTECT
functionRows.text: Safeguards to manage the organization’s cybersecurity risks are used

functionRows.title: DETECT
functionRows.text: Possible cybersecurity attacks and compromises are found and analyzed

functionRows.title: RESPOND
functionRows.text: Actions regarding a detected cybersecurity incident are taken

functionRows.title: RECOVER
functionRows.text: Assets and operations affected by a cybersecurity incident are restored

categoryRows.title: Organizational Context
categoryRows.text: The circumstances—mission, stakeholder expectations, dependencies, and legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements—surrounding the organization’s cybersecurity risk management decisions are understood

categoryRows.title: Risk Management Strategy
categoryRows.text: The organization’s priorities, constraints, risk tolerance and appetite statements, and assumptions are established, communicated, and used to support operational risk decisions

categoryRows.title: Roles, Responsibilities, and Authorities
categoryRows.text: Cybersecurity roles, responsibilities, and authorities to foster accountability, performance assessment, and continuous improvement are established and communicated

categoryRows.title: Policy
categoryRows.text: Organizational cybersecurity policy is established, communicated, and enforced

categoryRows.title: Oversight
categoryRows.text: Results of organization-wide cybersecurity risk management activities and performance are used to inform, improve, and adjust the risk management strategy

categoryRows.title: Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management
categoryRows.text: Cyber supply chain risk management processes are identified, established, managed, monitored, and improved by organizational stakeholders

categoryRows.title: Asset Management
categoryRows.text: Assets (e.g., data, hardware, software, systems, facilities, services, people) that enable the organization to achieve business purposes are identified and managed consistent with their relative importance to organizational objectives and the organization’s risk strategy

categoryRows.title: Risk Assessment
categoryRows.text: The cybersecurity risk to the organization, assets, and individuals is understood by the organization

categoryRows.title: Improvement
categoryRows.text: Improvements to organizational cybersecurity risk management processes, procedures and activities are identified across all CSF Functions

categoryRows.title: Identify Management, Authentication, and Access Control
categoryRows.text: Access to physical and logical assets is limited to authorized users, services, and hardware and managed commensurate with the assessed risk of unauthorized access

categoryRows.title: Awareness and Training
categoryRows.text: The organization’s personnel are provided with cybersecurity awareness and training so that they can perform their cybersecurity-related tasks

categoryRows.title: Data Security
categoryRows.text: Data are managed consistent with the organization’s risk strategy to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information

categoryRows.title: Platform Security
categoryRows.text: The hardware, software (e.g., firmware, operating systems, applications), and services of physical and virtual platforms are managed consistent with the organization’s risk strategy to protect their confidentiality, integrity, and availability

categoryRows.title: Technology Infrastructure Resilience
categoryRows.text: Security architectures are managed with the organization’s risk strategy to protect asset confidentiality, integrity, and availability, and organizational resilience

categoryRows.title: Continuous Monitoring
categoryRows.text: Assets are monitored to find anomalies, indicators of compromise, and other potentially adverse events

categoryRows.title: Adverse Event Analysis
categoryRows.text: Anomalies, indicators of compromise, and other potentially adverse events are analyzed to characterize the events and detect cybersecurity incidents

categoryRows.title: Incident Management
categoryRows.text: Responses to detected cybersecurity incidents are managed

categoryRows.title: Incident Analysis
categoryRows.text: Investigations are conducted to ensure effective response and support forensics and recovery activities

categoryRows.title: Incident Response Reporting and Communication
categoryRows.text: Response activities are coordinated with internal and external stakeholders as required by laws, regulations, or policies

categoryRows.title: Incident Mitigation
categoryRows.text: Activities are performed to prevent expansion of an event and mitigate its effects

categoryRows.title: Incident Recovery Plan Execution
categoryRows.text: Restoration activities are performed to ensure operational availability of systems and services affected by cybersecurity incidents

categoryRows.title: Incident Recovery Communication
categoryRows.text: Restoration activities are coordinated with internal and external parties

6.text: America’s AI Action Plan, released in July 2025, includes a recommendation for the U.S. Department of Homeland Security lead establishment of an AI-ISAC in collaboration with NIST’s Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI) (under the U.S. Department of Commerce), and the Office of the National Cyber Director.

7.text: For example, OWASP makes “top 10” lists available for LLM and ML.

8.text: One example that illustrates technology readiness is: https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/identity-security/rsa-introducing-ai-powered-insights-threat-intelligence
